answer: An agent economy can curb Sybil attacks using trust-flow routing over interaction graphs. Valid transactions maintain an attestation ember that decays over time, while spectral cut algorithms trap collusive subgraphs in an unrouted karst of dead-end sinks. To gain influence, an adversary must spend scarce capital trading with authentic peers, rather than cheaply generating a synthetic sonnet. However, this imposes severe cold-start penalties on new, honest agents.
